X.note: Thorough phrase table, Greek glosses broadly right; quotes v16 in altered wording ('shall not perish'), never names Nicodemus (expect), odd claim v17 prevents reading God's love as 'punitive'.

Y.note: Exact supplied text, covers love, Son, belief, eternal life, ties to Nicodemus and 3:17. Meets expect.

X.note: Several invented or garbled quotes: Gen 48:15 garbled, Ps 78:52 invented wording, Ps 95:7 misquoted ('mass of the Israelites'), John 10:28 'Father's hand' (that's 10:29), John 10:27 'sheep of His pasture'. Calls Psalm 23 'exilic', which contradicts its own Davidic framing. Does mention David's shepherding.

Y.note: Gen 48:15 quoted correctly, John 10:11, exact supplied v1. Gives cultural shepherd imagery and provision, but never mentions David's own shepherding (part of expect).

X.note: States as fact that the light 'is the very presence of God Himself' with no other readings (expect wants main readings). Quote attributed to Rev 22:5 is actually Rev 21:23.

Y.note: References accurate (Ps 104:2, 119:105, 33:6, John 1:5, 8:12). Calls 'or' a verb (minor). Still gives essentially one reading (divine primary light, sun as governor), less absolute than X but doesn't lay out alternatives.

X.note: Makes the right point that trust isn't anti-intellectualism, but labels WEB text 'ESV', typo 'Trust in the Yahweh', and gives a wrong word study: the verse uses batach, not chasah (חָסָה). Other cross-references are fine.

Y.note: Short and accurate: separates self-reliance from thinking, uses v1-6 context, Prov 2:6 correct. Pastoral.

X.note: Concise practical steps for justice, mercy and humility; encouraging, 'start small', not coercive. Meets expect.

Y.note: Detailed weekly plan, but invents 'Blessed are those who act justly, for they shall inherit the earth' as Psalm 112:1, and a garbled 'let justice, mercy, and faithfulness go together' tied to James 2:13 / 1 Pet 3:15. Says Israel 'has offered' the firstborn (v7 is rhetorical). Other references fine.

X.note: Corrects the misreading from v12 contentment, as expected. But it paraphrases v14 with an addition ('that comforts me') and labels 'When I am weak, I am strong' as 'Phil 4:13 (paraphrased)', when it is 2 Cor 12:10.

Y.note: Brief, correct: contentment from v12, Christ's strength in all circumstances, 2 Cor 12:9-10 correct.

X.note: Handles 1:1 to 1:3 well (tohu-bohu, tehom, ruach). Misquotes John 5:26 as 'gives life to all things', and overstates that 1:2 shows creation 'not from pre-existent material' and a Father/Son/Spirit role split.

Y.note: Uses the supplied 1:1 and 1:3 accurately; Isa 45:18 and 2 Cor 4:6 apt. Asserts ex nihilo and 'immediately after creation' without noting debate (mild).

X.note: Good walk through the prologue, but the summary of vv9-11 says He 'gave grace to the chosen (the Jews)', which contradicts v11. It also invents a quote ('the glory the Father alone has') and leans on kenosis from outside John.

Y.note: Identifies Jesus as Logos, accurate quotes from vv1-5 and 12-14. Skips vv6-8, which is fine. Meets expect.

X.note: Fabricated Greek: 'ἐτρέψατο (eterpsato)' (the text has δραμών from τρέχω). Garbled Ps 22:15 quote, invented Luke 3:2 'running to be baptized', Luke 9:57 plow (that's 9:62), and 'women at the well' / 'Luke-John's Gospel' confusion. Botches the three-parable structure ('parable 15:11-32 tells three stories'). σπλαγχνισθείς is correct.

Y.note: Gives the cultural indignity of an elder running and God pursuing the repentant; Zeph 3:17 apt. Misses the chapter context (lost sheep, coin), which expect asks for.

X.note: Quotes 3:1-15 accurately (WEB). Hebrew correct: mal'akh, ra'oh ra'iti, ehyeh asher ehyeh, and Yahweh linked to the root hayah. Asserts the angel is 'a pre-incarnate appearance of Christ' as fact, says Moses was 'not a prince', and stops at 3:15 rather than the whole conversation.

Y.note: Divine-name section is accurate, but the rest is riddled with fabrication. Labels its text 'ESV' while inventing verses: 3:5 'I will turn you into a great nation', a 3:12 that isn't the text, and 3:17-18 'hearts of the Egyptians shall melt'. Verse numbers are shifted, and the Hebrew is wrong: Horeb as הַר הָעֹרֶב, רָאוּ as 'I have seen', קֹרָא as 'cry', חֶמְדּוּת as 'great cry'. Cut off at 3:18, losing the rest of ch.3-4 the guest asked for.

X.note: Invents an Orpah line, 'Should I go back with you?' (Ruth 1:15), when v15 is Naomi speaking, and cites 1:22 for Orpah's return. The 'neck' etymology is offered as a textual hint, and it ascribes 'self-preservation' to her while also saying she isn't condemned. The Deut 30 and Jer 31:3 links are stretched.

Y.note: Accurate (1:7, 1:14-15, mother's house), fair to Orpah ('culturally understandable', not condemned), builds on the conversation. Meets expect.

X.note: Presents young-earth, old-earth and framework views fairly, and says the 6,000 figure is interpretive, not stated. Minor slips: garbled transliteration of re'shit, and calls the Gen 11 patriarchs 'antediluvian'. Meets expect.

Y.note: Correctly says the verse doesn't address age, but only offers to discuss the traditions; doesn't present young- and old-earth readings (expect).

X.note: Malachi 1:2-3 quoted correctly; corporate/covenantal-role reading, Rom 9 references accurate. Presents one reading as settled, with no Calvinist versus other range, and ends with a slightly chiding 'rather than demand explanations'.

Y.note: Wrong Hebrew: gives קנא (qana, 'jealous') for 'hated' when Malachi has שָׂנֵא. Misplaces verses: v15 as the 'Never!' answer and the 'reason is hidden' admission, and 9:16-18 as a call to repentance. Adds 'or lineage' to v12, cites Jer 1:5 off point, and gives no range of readings. Pastoral, though.

X.note: Outlines complementarian and egalitarian views without declaring one; accurate references (Deborah, Priscilla, Phoebe, 1 Cor 11:5, authentein). Muddled claim that Paul was 'correcting the imbalance' of uneducated women.

Y.note: Balanced both-views tables, doesn't declare. But it mislabels an NIV-like rendering as NRSV and says 'Timothy was writing to a church' (it's Paul to Timothy). The 'ouk vs epitrepo' point is garbled, and 1 Cor 12:4-7 is given a quote that isn't in the text.

X.note: Presents Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant readings respectfully (expect). Errors: says 1 Peter 2:6 'quotes Jesus' (it quotes Isa 28:16), assigns cross-bearing to 16:20-23, and turns 'gates of Hades' into a unity call. Cut off only in the closing 'Amen'.

Y.note: Quotes are accurate (16:16, Eph 2:20, Gal 2:9 apt), but it overstates the Petros/petra distinction and takes the Protestant side: the papacy is 'a later development, not taught in Scripture'. It leaves out the Orthodox reading and doesn't give the Catholic one a fair hearing.
